newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline trades mixed in two-tier barge market.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline trades mixed in two-tier barge market.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were mixed on Thursday as widely varied barge trades confused the cargo market ahead of the NYMEX open, traders said.

Tighter barge supplies were seen temporarily offsetting a weaker cargo market, where a closed arbitrage to the States and healthy offers by at least three sellers were putting a cap on prices, they said.
Eurograde barges for fob ARA were assessed from $187 to $190 while Rotterdam refinery material was quoted higher at $191 to $193, after an early bid and offer at $195 and $197, traders said.
Two U.S.-based traders continued to dominate the barge market, with one a noted buyer and the other a seller.
A trader at a major put premium unleaded cargo prices at $183 fob and $193 cif, based on barge prices at roughly $188.
He expected cargo prices to fall the rest of the week due to the closed arbitrage and sellers looking to Europe instead of the States.
July NYMEX unleaded gasoline traded between 56.55 and 56.95 cents a gallon in overnight ACCESS trading, up slightly from its close on Wednesday at 56.54 cents.

Gasoline inventories held in independent tankage in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp area fell in the week ended on Thursday, as cargoes moved to other NWE ports and barge movements were balanced, according to industry sources.
Stocks fell to 425-450,000 tonnes from 475,000 tonnes the previous week, but were above the year-ago level of 350-375,000 tonnes.
